tagline: From a 602-foot dam to the towns that built it.
intro: Shasta Dam Boulevard starts at the visitor center south of Shasta Dam, a concrete wall 602 feet high that holds the Sacramento River back as Shasta Lake, the largest reservoir in California. The stretch across the top of the dam is closed to the public. The state road heads south instead, a little over three miles through heavily vegetated country to Lake Boulevard.

The towns along it came with the dam. In 1938 the government built Toyon for its staff on a farm here, and allowed no stores or restaurants. Makeshift camps called Central Valley, Project City and Summit City filled with men from all over the state hoping for work.

moments.title: Shasta Dam
moments.text: Tours run all year, with a 428-foot elevator ride down to the base. Behind the dam, the copper town of Kennett went under the rising lake within five years of the groundbreaking.

moments.title: Shasta Lake
moments.text: The construction camps grew into the city of Shasta Lake. Summit City stood at the end of this road, where Shasta Dam Boulevard meets Lake Boulevard.
